title: Identifying Hub Genes Related to Vascular Endothelial Cell Permeability Through Bioinformatics and Verification.
authors: Zheng, Yunjiang; Chen, Qianyi; Cao, Lei; Zhao, Lili; Tang, Yi; Liu, Zhihan
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生物信息学筛选血管内皮细胞通透性相关枢纽基因，核心是基因表达与PPI网络分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: In this study, we aimed to identify the hub genes responsible for increased vascular endothelial cell permeability. METHODS: We applied the weighted Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database to mine dataset GSE178331 and ob-tained the most relevant high-throughput sequenced genes for an increased permeability of vascular endothelial cells due to inflammation. We constructed two weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) networks, and the differential expression of high-throughput sequenced genes related to endothelial cell permeability were screened from the GEO database. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis were performed on the differential genes. Their degree values were obtained from the topological properties of protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks of differential genes, and the hub genes associated with an increased endothelial cell permeability were analyzed. Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and western blotting techniques were used to detect the presence of these hub genes in TNF-alpha induced mRNA and the protein expression in endothelial cells. RESULTS: In total, 1,475 differential genes were mainly enriched in the cell adhesion and TNF-alpha signaling pathway. With TNF-alpha inducing an increase in the endothelial cell permeability and significantly increasing mRNA and protein expression levels, we identified three hub genes, namely PTGS2, ICAM1, and SNAI1. There was a significant difference in the high-dose TNF-alpha group and in the low-dose TNF-alpha group compared to the control group, in the endothelial cell permeability experiment (p = 0.008 vs. p = 0.02). Measurement of mRNA and protein levels of PTGS2, ICAM1, and SNAI1 by western blotting analysis showed that there was a significant impact on TNF-alpha and that there was a significant dose-dependent relationship (p < 0.05 vs. p < 0.01). CONCLUSIONS: The three hub genes identified through bioinformatics analyses in the present study may serve as biomarkers of increased vascular endothelial cell permeability. The findings offer valuable insights into the progress and mechanism of vascular endothelial cell permeability.
abstract_zh: 背景：在本研究中，我们旨在识别导致血管内皮细胞通透性增加的核心基因。方法：我们应用加权基因表达综合（Gene Expression Omnibus, GEO）数据库挖掘数据集GSE178331，并获取与炎症引起的血管内皮细胞通透性增加最相关的高通量测序基因。我们构建了两个加权基因共表达网络分析（weighted gene co-expression network analysis, WGCNA）网络，并从GEO数据库中筛选出与内皮细胞通透性相关的高通量测序基因的差异表达。对差异基因进行了基因本体论（Gene Ontology, GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, KEGG）富集分析。从差异基因的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（protein-protein interaction, PPI）网络的拓扑性质中获取其度值，并分析与内皮细胞通透性增加相关的核心基因。采用逆转录聚合酶链反应（reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction, RT-PCR）和蛋白质印迹技术检测这些核心基因在TNF-α诱导的mRNA及内皮细胞中蛋白表达的存在。结果：总共1,475个差异基因主要富集于细胞粘附和TNF-α信号通路。在TNF-α诱导内皮细胞通透性增加并显著提高mRNA和蛋白表达水平的情况下，我们识别出三个核心基因，即PTGS2、ICAM1和SNAI1。在内皮细胞通透性实验中，与对照组相比，高剂量TNF-α组和低剂量TNF-α组均存在显著差异（p = 0.008 vs. p = 0.02）。通过蛋白质印迹分析测量PTGS2、ICAM1和SNAI1的mRNA和蛋白水平显示，TNF-α有显著影响，且存在显著的剂量依赖性关系（p < 0.05 vs. p < 0.01）。结论：本研究中通过生物信息学分析识别的三个核心基因可能作为血管内皮细胞通透性增加的生物标志物。这些发现为血管内皮细胞通透性的进展和机制提供了有价值的见解。
